card.name: Belly dance
card.era: ancient roots; term coined 1860s; Egyptian classical form 20th century
card.tagline: Torso-driven dance of hip and abdomen articulations
card.profile: Belly dance is the Western name (from the French danse du ventre, coined in the 1860s) for a torso-driven dance emphasising articulations of the hips and torso, with Egypt's forms the most recognised worldwide. Per Wikipedia, in Egypt it has two contexts: the social/folk raqs baladi danced by ordinary people at celebrations, and the professional raqs sharqi of cabarets and film. It isolates the torso muscles rather than moving the limbs through space, distinguishing it from many Western dance forms.
card.insight: Belly dance is among the most globally widespread Middle Eastern dance forms, though it remains contested within parts of the Arab world; Egyptian cinema spread its imagery worldwide (Wikipedia).

lessons.title: Beginners Bellydance Tutorial | By Leilah Isaac

parts.note: Introduction to the beginners belly dance workout and channel info
Explanation of basic posture, feet alignment, pelvis neutral position, and upper body stance
Full-body stretching warm-up with arm reaches and plie squat variations
Detailed breakdown of side, back, and forward hip stretches and isolations
Slower practice of upper body stretches and side-to-side rib isolation
Instruction on hip shifting outside normal body alignment
Leg lifts, ankle circles, and toe points for strengthening

steps.name: Basic Posture
steps.description: Feet under hips, knees slightly bent, pelvis in mid neutral position, shoulders back, chest lifted.

steps.name: Plie Stretch Warmup
steps.description: In and release plie with arms crossing and extending overhead.

steps.name: Hip Side Stretch
steps.description: Squeezing and pushing hip to one side with knees bent for glute stretch.

steps.name: Hip Shifts
steps.description: Shifting hips side to side outside regular alignment with chest still.

images: Imagine river flowing from your hands
Pelvis has a mind of the road
common_mistakes: Bending forward instead of keeping posture
Arching pelvis too far under or back
Slanted side-to-side movement instead of pulling
safety: Do not worry how far you can go today, your body will improve
lessons.teacher_style: Leilah guides beginners through gentle full-body warmups with detailed postural alignment and continuous encouragement. She breaks down isolation movements step-by-step, focusing on flexibility and muscle conditioning.
lessons.distinctive_method: Extensive use of visualization (e.g., river flowing from hands, pelvis having a mind of the road) paired with physical isolation holds.
what_works: Clear verbal explanations of posture and body mechanics
Repetitive practice from multiple angles including mirror
what_hinders: Long verbal explanations during static holding positions

evidence.observation: Teacher stands facing front in a room with a large mirror, gesturing while speaking.
